H.A.L.O. — High Altitude Launch Operations

We are H.A.L.O., a team driven by curiosity, engineering, and the ambition to push beyond the limits of Earth. Combining technical thinking with creative problem-solving, we turn complex aerospace challenges into working solutions. Our mission is to explore, design, and build technologies that bring humanity closer to the stars.

Beyond the atmosphere. Beyond expectations.

summary: We have developed a simple game in which the user must monitor the status of a base and complete missions to earn points. As required, the game includes an energy budget, mission management, and other decisions that must be made urgently. We believe this is important because it can spark children's interest and encourage them to pursue a future in the aerospace field.
details:
H.A.L.O. is an interactive learning game that lets children manage a lunar outpost for 30 mission days. Players balance electricity, life support, food, water, crew health, and radiation protection. They respond to situations such as solar storms, dust on solar panels, power failures, water leaks, and oxygen leaks. Every decision has a trade-off. For example, raising the radiation shield protects the crew but uses battery power that is also needed for life support.

The project helps young learners understand that space missions depend on teamwork, planning, limited resources, and quick engineering decisions. Instead of memorizing facts in a quiz, players learn through consequences inside a safe simulation. The intended impact is to make STEM and space exploration more engaging for children aged 7–12, while encouraging problem solving, responsibility, and curiosity about real NASA missions.

We developed the game with Godot 4 and GDScript. It uses a 3D lunar environment created with KayKit Space Base and Prototype assets, plus NASA LRO/LOLA lunar-terrain data. The space-weather scenarios are based on an offline, child-friendly archive inspired by NASA DONKI data about solar flares, coronal mass ejections, and solar energetic particle events. The game can run locally or be exported for a web browser, so it does not require special hardware.

H.A.L.O. is creative because it turns real mission risks into understandable gameplay. It combines a lunar-base simulator, a friendly visual style, real scientific context, bilingual English/Russian text, onboarding guidance, and an optional Sudoku easter egg. The team considered accessibility for younger players, readable controls, safe offline data use, balanced difficulty, browser performance, and the need to clearly distinguish game values from real safety or radiation forecasts.
